Dub
DUB
noun (Gen-Z slang)
From the spoken name of the letter W ("double-u," shortened to "dub"), the win column in sports records. "Get the dub" and "take the dub" spread through sports talk, hip-hop, and especially Fortnite and other online games in the late 2010s. Distinct from the older verbs dub (to knight; to name) and dub (to add a soundtrack or translation).

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang a dub is a win: a victory in a game, a good grade, a small success. "We got the dub." "Huge dub." It is the opposite of an L. The Christian observation: Scripture is not shy about victory. The Psalms celebrate battles won, Paul uses athletic contests freely — "So run, that ye may obtain" (1Co 9:24) — and the Christian is "more than conquerors through him that loved us" (Rom 8:37). Wanting to win is not a sin. But Scripture is careful about whose dub it is. The race is not finally "to the swift, nor the battle to the strong... but time and chance happeneth to them all" (Ecc 9:11); every earthly win is a gift and a temporary one. Paul contrasts the athlete’s "corruptible crown" with the believer’s "incorruptible" one (1Co 9:25). And the greatest dub is not ours at all: "thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ" (1Co 15:57); "this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith" (1Jn 5:4). A father celebrates his son’s dubs on the field and teaches him to say thank you for them — and to remember the one victory that cannot be lost.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (from "double-u," the W of a win record; gaming, late 2010s) for a win — victories Scripture celebrates as gifts, beneath the victory God gives in Christ.

expand to see more

DUB, n. (Gen-Z slang; from the letter W, "double-u") A win, a victory, a success. "Got the dub tonight." "That’s a huge dub."

Also W alone: "W," "big W," "W friend." Opposite: L (see Take the L).

Older, unrelated senses: dub, to confer knighthood or a name; to add sound to film; British dubs, twenty-inch wheels.

Webster (1828), root word dub: “DUB, verb transitive [&hellip;] Literally, to strike. Hence, 1. To strike a blow with a sword, and make a knight. Se cyng, dubbade his sunu Henric to ridere. The King dubbed his son Henry a knight. 2. To confer any dignity or new character. A man of wealth is dubbd a man of worth.”

Decode for parents: a win. Celebrate it, and teach thanksgiving for it.

Key Scripture

1Co 15:57 — "But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ."

Rom 8:37 — "Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us."

1Jn 5:4 — "For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith."

Ecc 9:11 — "I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all."

1Co 9:25 — "And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible."

Modern Corruption

Dub is honest delight in winning; its drift is only the scoreboard heart that lives for the next W, where Scripture receives every win as a gift and rests in the victory God gives in Christ.

expand to see more

Winning is good, and Scripture uses races and contests to describe the Christian life (1Co 9:24–25). The drift is a heart that measures every day in Ws and Ls — ranked matches, likes, grades, girls — and feels worthless after a loss. The Preacher punctured that long ago: the race is not always to the swift, "but time and chance happeneth to them all" (Ecc 9:11).

The believer has a win that is not on the board. "Thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory" (1Co 15:57); "this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith" (1Jn 5:4). Teach your son to chase dubs hard, to thank God for each one, and to know that his biggest dub was won for him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Letter W ("double-u") in sports records → spoken "dub" → hip-hop, sports talk, Fortnite (late 2010s) → Gen-Z word for any win.

Clipped to "dub" in sports and hip-hop talk

Gen-Z: "W" and "dub" for any success

Distinct from dub, to knight or to name (Old English dubbian)
